During descent, if the altitude constraint requires the aircraft to cross the waypoint AT the specified altitude, or AT OR ABOVE the specified altitude, the aircraft holds the specified altitude until arrival at the waypoint in FLC or PTCH descent mode. If the altitude constraint requires the aircraft to cross the waypoint BETWEEN two altitudes, the lower altitude is held. If the altitude constraint requires the aircraft to cross the waypoint AT OR BELOW the specified altitude, no altitude will be held.

During climb, if the altitude constraint requires the aircraft to cross the waypoint at the specified altitude, or requires the aircraft to cross the waypoint at or below the specified altitude, the specified altitude is held until the waypoint is reached. If the altitude constraint requires the aircraft to cross the waypoint between two altitudes, the higher altitude is held. If the altitude constraint requires the aircraft to cross the waypoint at or above the specified altitude, then there is no requirement to hold an altitude.

If the preselect altitude is not raised to the flight plan target altitude or above during climb, the preselected altitude will be captured, causing the mode to be sequenced to VALTS. When preselect altitude is eventually raised, VNAV will not sequence to climb VFLC until a climb mode selection is made.

The Altitude Hold Mode (ALT) is activated manually by pressing the ALT Button on the Flight Control Panel (FCP). After ALT Mode is activated, if no other vertical mode (FLC or VS Mode) has been selected, the aircraft will continue to climb/descend due to inertia, and then descend/climb again to capture the baro pressure altitude when ALT Mode is activated.

The OSPD Mode automatically activates when the aircraft's Mach number exceeds Mmo + 0.01 or airspeed exceeds Vmo + 5 kt, to generate pitch commands to reduce airspeed below Vmo/Mmo. The speed reference becomes Mmo - 0.02 or Vmo - 10 kt.

The USPD Mode is automatically activated when aircraft airspeed is less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach is less than Mman - 0.01, unless ALTS mode is captured or ALT mode is active. An amber USPD symbol is displayed in the vertical Mode annunciation area of the FMA, and an aural alert "underspeed" is given. The AP and AT provide thrust/speed commands to prevent stall stick shaker by generating pitch commands to increase airspeed above Vman or Mman. The SPEED Knob is inhibited when USPD mode is active, and other vertical modes are inhibited unless in ALTS Mode (including ALTS CAP), ALT Mode, TO Mode and GA Mode. AT is armed when the system operates in USPD Mode. The USPD Mode can be deselected when airspeed is more than Vman - 5 kt or Mman - 0.01 M, or if the airspeed increases to Vman/Mman, at which point the USPD Mode exits automatically, airspeed reference is set to Vman + 5 kt/Mman + 0.01, the FG vertical Mode switches to FLC Mode, and the current altitude reference remains. Underspeed Protection Mode is inhibited below 1000 ft after takeoff and after GS capture during ILS approach, and will not be activated in ALT or ALTS Mode in cruise phase.

The following conditions show up as Amber:
* **DOORS > Door Status:** The corresponding door is not locked or the sensor fails.
* **ELECTRICAL > L/R GEN Status and Output Indication:** TRU fails.
* **ELECTRICAL > APU GEN Status and Output Indication:** APU fails.
* **ELECTRICAL > EXT PWR Status and Output Indication:** The status of the corresponding generator is displayed in amber or the load of the corresponding generator is more than 100%.
* **ELECTRICAL > BUS (L AC, R AC, L DC, R DC and AC 3PH ESS):** Bus fault.
* **ELECTRICAL > TRU Status and Output Indication:** The corresponding TRU fails.
* **ELECTRICAL > MAIN BATT and APU BATT Status and Parameters:** MAIN (APU) BATT DISCHARGE or MAIN (APU) BATT FAULT or MAIN (APU) BATT TEMP SENS FAULT message are displayed on EICAS.
* **ELECTRICAL > Flight Control Battery:** Flight control battery fault.
* **ELECTRICAL > RAT GEN Status and Output Indication:** RAT OVERLOAD message is displayed on EICAS.
* **ELECTRICAL > Static Inverter:** The INVERTER FAULT message is displayed on EICAS.
* **COMMUNICATIONS > SELCAL System Indication:** SELCAL code available but not matched, or difference between SELCAL codes detected by different sources, or SELCAL code is set to AAAA.
* **NAVIGATION > Radio Altitude Displays on the PFD:** Decision height is set. When the aircraft reaches the decision height, radio altitude value is displayed in amber and MINIMUMS aural alert sounds. When there is a difference beyond limit between the two RA values, the values are displayed in amber beside.
* **INDICATING/RECORDING > Definitions of Colors:** Caution, caution level crew alert messages and abnormal source annunciations.

The TO Mode can be deselected in any of the following ways: – Changing the FG coupled side. – Manually selecting other lateral modes. – Manually selecting other vertical modes.

The Go-around (GA) Mode can be selected by pressing the TOGA Pushbutton when the aircraft is in flight. This action disengages the Autopilot (AP), sets the Autothrottle (AT) to go-around thrust (engaging it automatically if disengaged), and activates the Flight Directors (FDs) on both sides. The GA Mode will deselect any other vertical mode.
Lateral GA Mode can be deselected by changing the coupled side or manually selecting other lateral modes. Vertical GA Mode can be deselected by changing the coupled side or manually selecting other vertical modes. The AP can be deselected by pressing the SYNC Pushbutton on either side.
During GA Mode, the pitch angle is commanded according to the go-around target speed, with an initial lower limit of 8° reducing to 4°. The FD pitch command upper limit expands to 30°, while the AP pitch control upper limit remains at 20°. The go-around target speed is the greater of VAPP or the current speed, ranging from VREF + 5 kt to VREF + 20 kt for two-engine operation, and VREF + 5 kt to VREF + 15 kt for single-engine operation.
The Automatic Takeoff Thrust Control System (ATTCS) is automatically engaged during the Go-Around Phase, regardless of the ATTCS Inhibit Switch position.

The OSPD Mode is automatically activated when the aircraft's Mach number exceeds Mmo + 0.01 or its airspeed exceeds Vmo + 5 kt. In this mode, the Autopilot (AP) and Autothrottle (AT) provide pitch and thrust/speed commands to prevent the aircraft speed from exceeding Vmo/Mmo, with a speed reference of Mmo - 0.02 or Vmo - 10 kt.

The USPD Mode is automatically activated when aircraft airspeed is less than Vman - 5 kt or Mach is less than Mman - 0.01. It generates pitch commands to increase airspeed above Vman or Mman. The mode exits automatically when airspeed/Mach is greater than Vman/Mman, and the airspeed reference is set to Vman + 5 kt/Mman + 0.01. The SPEED Knob is inhibited when USPD mode is active, and AT is armed. USPD is inhibited below 1000 ft after takeoff, after GS capture during ILS approach, and will not activate in ALT or ALTS Mode during cruise.

The Windshear Escape Mode (WS) is automatically entered when the TAWS detects a windshear warning. It provides optimal escape maneuver commands by integrating airspeed, radio altitude, and AOA data until the windshear warnings cease. The autopilot disengages automatically after 2 seconds, and the thrust is set to TOGA. To manually exit WS Mode, another vertical mode must be selected.

In Automatic Refueling Mode, set the REFUEL SELECTION Switch to AUTO. Use the INCR/DECRT Switch to set the required refuel quantity. Manually open the Refuel Shutoff Valve to start. The Fuel Quantity Computer (FQC) monitors and automatically closes the valve when the preselected quantity is reached, ensuring balanced fuel quantities between left and right tanks. The FQC automatically records the last preselected refuel quantity. To activate automatic mode, the INCR/DECRT Switch must be operated even if the required quantity matches the displayed value. The FQC balances tanks by shutting off the tank with more fuel if the imbalance exceeds 400 kg (882 lb) and resumes refueling both when balanced. Refueling also stops when tanks reach maximum quantity via the High Level Float Pilot Valve.

The CDU provides remote tuning for COM, NAV, DME, ADF, HF, and ATC radios. It can tune radios by transmitting requests to the RTU or directly to the transceiver if both RTUs are inoperative. Remote tuning uses a two-level page system: a top-level Radio TUNE page for overall frequency control and secondary control pages for individual radios. On the Radio TUNE page, active frequencies can be entered into the scratchpad and transferred using LSK L1 or R1, while preset frequencies can be entered into the scratchpad and tuned using LSK L2 or R2. Preset frequencies can also be recalled by pressing LSK L2 or R2 without data in the scratchpad. On individual COM control pages, active frequencies are set with LSK L1, and preset/recall frequencies are activated with LSK L2. LSK R1 allows switching between preset frequency pages and airport frequency lookup pages. The airport frequency lookup allows searching for COM frequencies associated with a given airport using four airport identifiers: Departure, Arrival, Alternate, and Pilot Entered.

V1 (Takeoff Decision Speed) is the speed from which a decision to continue takeoff, following a failure of the critical engine at VEF, results in a takeoff distance to a height of 35 ft at V2 speed not exceeding the takeoff distance available (TODA), or, in case of rejected takeoff, the distance to bring the aircraft to a full stop not exceeding the accelerate-stop distance available (ASDA). VR (Rotation Speed) is the speed from which a decision to continue the takeoff, following a failure of the critical engine at VEF, results in a takeoff distance to a height of 35 ft at V2 speed. V2 (Takeoff Safety Speed) is the target speed to be attained at the 35 ft height, assuming recognition of one engine failure at V1 and the decision to continue is taken. VFTO (Last Takeoff Speed) is the last takeoff safety speed reached at the end of the takeoff flight path, which is a fixed value of 220 kt.

The vertical modes are engaged and disengaged through the related pushbuttons on the Flight Control Panel (FCP).

In Automatic Refueling Mode, set the REFUEL SELECTION Switch to AUTO. Use the INCR/DECRT Switch to set the required refuel quantity. Manually open the Refuel Shutoff Valve to start refueling. The Fuel Quantity Computer (FQC) monitors the process and automatically closes the Refuel Shutoff Valve when the preselected quantity is reached. The FQC automatically records and displays the last preselected refuel quantity. To activate the FQC and enter Automatic Refueling Mode, it is necessary to operate the INCR/DECRT Switch, even if the required quantity is the same as displayed. This mode ensures fuel quantities between left and right tanks are balanced upon completion. If an imbalance of more than 400 kg (882 lb) occurs, the FQC shuts off the valve in the tank with the higher quantity. When balanced, both tanks are refueled. Refueling is completed when the combined total equals the preselected value. Regardless of the mode, the High Level Float Pilot Valve will close the Refuel Shutoff Valve when the aircraft reaches maximum quantity.

The FQC does not automatically record. The Flight Data Recorder (FDR) system records aircraft flight parameters. The Wireless Quick Access Recorder (WQAR) stores and records aircraft system parameters transmitted by the Real-time Monitoring Unit (RTMU).

RTU Tuning is done by selecting the tuning window via the Line Select Key (LSK) and rotating the concentric tune knobs. There are four tuning methods available: direct tuning, standby tuning, preset tuning and remote tuning.

The CDU provides remote tuning function for COM, NAV, DME, ADF, HF and ATC. It can tune radios via the RTU or directly to the transceiver if both RTUs are inoperative. To tune, press the TUNE key on the CDU to access the Radio TUNE page. From there, you can enter active or preset frequencies, recall preset frequencies, and access secondary control pages for individual radios like COM1. The airport frequency lookup feature allows searching for COM frequencies associated with a given airport. The system also supports auto tuning commands from the FMS routed through the radio tuning system application in the IPC. It is recommended to use the RTU for tuning, but if using the CDU, ensure Remote Tuning (RMT) is on and allow sufficient time between CDU operations and RTU operations (or subsequent CDU operations) to avoid synchronization issues or errors. If an RTU fails, the operational RTU takes over. If both RTUs fail, the CDU handles tuning for both sides.

**EICAS Inhibition Logic:**
*   **Power-up Phase (T0a):** From power-up to one engine start.
*   **Start Phase (T0b):** From one engine start to takeoff thrust of both engines, and airspeed reaching 40 kt.
*   **Takeoff phase 1 (T1):** From the takeoff thrust of both engines and airspeed over 40 kt to the airspeed reaching 100 kt.
*   **Takeoff phase 2 (T2):** From 100 kt to 1500 ft RA or 120 s after lift-off, whichever comes first.
*   **Landing Phase (L):** From 800 ft RA to 40 kt or when on ground for 30 s.

**TCAS Alert Inhibits:**
*   **Resolution Advisory (RA) Descent (1500 ft/min):** Inhibited below 1100 ft AGL during climb or below 900 ft AGL during descend.
*   **Resolution Advisory (RA) Descent (2500 ft/min):** Inhibited below 1200 ft AGL during climb or below 1000 ft AGL during descend.
*   **Accelerated Resolution Advisory (RA) Descent:** Inhibited below 1650 ft AGL during climb or below 1450 ft AGL during descend.

**TAWS G/S Inhibit Conditions:**

V2 (Takeoff Safety Speed) is the target speed to be attained at the 35 ft height, assuming recognition of one engine failure at V1 and the decision to continue is taken. VFTO (Last Takeoff Speed) is the last takeoff safety speed reached at the end of the takeoff flight path.

When the relative position of the intruder presents a collision threat, aural and visual alerts are triggered.
The different classifications of intruders in TCAS are Proximate traffic, Traffic Advisory (TA), and Resolution Advisory (RA).
Proximate traffic is identified as traffic within 6 NM laterally and ± 1200 ft vertically. It is displayed on the PFD/MFD as a filled cyan diamond.

Traffic Advisory (TA) informs the pilot of proximate traffic which does not constitute a threat at present but may become a threat when conditions change. The Time To UA (TAU) for a TA is about 40 seconds.

TAWS displays terrain using solid amber for CPA cautions, solid red for CPA warnings (Pull Up), and red-and-black "X" for CPA warnings (Terrain Avoidance). TAWS provides visual and aural alerts for conditions such as CPA cautions/warnings for obstacles and terrain, excessive rate of descent, dangerous proximity to terrain, altitude decreases during takeoff/go-around, incorrect landing configuration with insufficient terrain clearance, excessive G/S deviation, excessive bank angle, and altitude callouts. It also provides windshear cautions and warnings.
Resolution Advisory (RA) is a real collision threat with a Time to lose (TAU) of about 25 s.

The Flap/Slat Control System controls three leading-edge slats and two trailing-edge flaps for each wing. These are electrically controlled and actuated high-lift devices used to increase wing lift and decrease stall speed during takeoff, maneuvering, and landing. The system incorporates skew and asymmetry protection, where Power Drive Units (PDUs) stop operating and the system is cut out and locked if detected. The Flap/Slat Electronic Control Units (FSECUs) manage flap/slat position commands from the FLP/SLT Handle and send signals to the PDUs. The system also has an interlock function related to airspeed and ground conditions, and retraction/extension sequences for slats and flaps. Flaps and slats can be controlled via the FLP/SLT Handle or the FLP/SLT OVRD Switch. Flap/slat positions are displayed on the EICAS, with specific color coding for status (Green, Cyan, Amber). If the aircraft speed exceeds the placard speed for a selected detent, EICAS will display the "FLP/SLT PLACARD SPD" amber caution message. When the RAT is extended, flap/slat extension is limited to FLAP 3.

V1: Takeoff Decision Speed. The speed from which a decision to continue the takeoff, following a failure of the critical engine at VEF, results in a takeoff distance to a height of 35 ft at V2 speed not exceeding the takeoff distance available (TODA), or, in case of rejected takeoff, the distance to bring the aircraft to a full stop not exceed the accelerate-stop distance available (ASDA).
VR: Rotation Speed. The speed from which a decision to continue the takeoff, following a failure of the critical engine at VEF, results in a takeoff distance to a height of 35 ft at V2 speed.
V2: Takeoff Safety Speed. The target speed to be attained at the 35 ft height, assuming recognition of one engine failure at V1 and the decision to continue is taken.
VFTO: Last Takeoff Speed. The last takeoff safety speed reached at the end of the takeoff flight path.

In Automatic Refueling Mode, the REFUEL SELECTION Switch is set to AUTO. The INCR/DECRT Switch is used to set the required refuel quantity. The Refuel Shutoff Valve is manually selected open to start refueling. The main components of the air conditioning process include PACKs, a mixing manifold, and the trim air system.

The bleed air from the pneumatic system is adjusted through the two flow control valves, temperature and pressure are adjusted through two PACKs. Then the bleed air enters the mixing manifold where it is mixed with the recirculated air from the cabin. Hot trim air from the upstream of the PACK is mixed with the air from the mixing manifold in the air conditioning distribution duct, and then distributed to the cockpit and cabin to maintain selected temperature.

The Primary Actuator Control Electronics (P-ACE) receives input commands from the control column and control wheel and sensitivity signals from Flight Control Cabinet (FCC), then sends the signals to the Power Control Unit (PCU) to drive elevators, ailerons and rudder.

Stall Protection System provides stall alert, stall protection and auto-ignition functions.
Two Angle of Attack (AOA) Sensors integrated with Stall Protection Computers (SPC), one stick pusher integrated in AP pitch servo, and two stick shakers.

There are two Data Concentrator Units (DCUs) of EICAS. Each DCU has two channels, A and B. Channel B is used for airborne data concentration and routing, while channel A performs complex computing functions, data concentration, and routing. Channel A of both DCUs receives all aircraft data and can operate independently. Channel B sends data from its side of the aircraft systems to channel A of the opposite DCU. Data is internally routed to both channels within each DCU. The system separates left and right aircraft systems by routing them to the respective DCUs, with data required by both DCUs cross-referenced via a crossfeed bus.
Each FADEC channel can control two ignitors.
Each control column has one stick shaker and each Stall Protection Computer (SPC) can drive both stick shakers at the same time.

In Normal Mode, the primary flight control system uses airspeed for sensitivity scaling and limiting. Sensitivity scaling of the rudder depends on airspeed, engine fault status, flap position, and aircraft on the ground or in flight status. Elevator sensitivity scaling depends on airspeed and flap position, with maximum deflection limited on the ground below flap detent 2. Aileron and multi-function spoiler sensitivity scaling depends on airspeed. If CANCEL EXIT is selected and executed after the FMS initiates a turn to the inbound leg and does not exit the hold, it will continue the turn to the inbound leg and return to the FIX. After crossing the FIX, the FMS follows the complete holding pattern in the normal way. If the aircraft is in the inbound turn or leg before crossing the FIX when CANCEL EXIT is selected and executed, the FMS steers the aircraft around the holding pattern as if EXIT HOLD has not been selected. The FMS operate the aircraft to continue the hold in one of three ways: If an outbound turn is in progress, the FMS will complete the turn to the outbound leg and continue the hold. If an inbound turn is in progress, the FMS will complete the turn to the inbound leg and continue the hold. If the aircraft is on the inbound leg, the FMS will continue the hold as if the exit was never selected.

In Normal Mode, the primary flight control system uses airspeed for sensitivity scaling and limiting for rudder, elevator, aileron, and multi-function spoiler. The Bob Weight function increases control column pitch feel during high "G" loads. Force fight compensation reduces control surface force fights. Configuration Trim compensates for flap/slat or speedbrake changes by adjusting stabilizer position. Yaw Damping and Turn Coordination are calculated in the automatic flight control system. Mach Trim and Horizontal Stabilizer Auto Trim are also calculated in the automatic flight control system. Roll Assist and Roll/Speedbrake Mixer integrate speedbrake and roll assist commands. Ground Lift Dump automatically extends spoilers to decrease lift and increase weight on wheels during landing or rejected takeoff. Pitch trim rate is adjusted depending on airspeed.

The Engine Oil System provides oil for the engine bearings and the Accessory Gearbox. The APU uses an integral independent oil system to lubricate and cool the APU Generator, Gearbox assembly, and Rotor bearings. There are three fuel/oil heat exchangers: main fuel/oil heat exchanger, servo fuel/oil heat exchanger, and Integrated Drive Generator fuel/oil heat exchanger.

Refueling is normally done by pressure not exceeding 55 psi. It can also be done by gravity if pressure equipment is unavailable. There are two modes of pressure refueling: automatic and manual, selected via the REFUEL SELECTION Switch. The Fuel Quantity Computer (FQC) monitors automatic refueling, ensuring fuel balance between the left and right tanks. Refueling can be stopped manually even in automatic mode. Regardless of the mode, the High Level Float Pilot Valve stops refueling when the aircraft reaches maximum quantity. HF communication should not be used during refueling.

Sensitivity scaling of the rudder depends on airspeed, engine fault status, flap position, and aircraft on the ground or in flight status. Sensitivity scaling of the elevator depends on airspeed and flap position. When the aircraft is on the ground and flaps are below detent 2, the elevator cannot reach maximum deflection. Sensitivity scaling of the aileron and multi-function spoiler depends on airspeed. In Normal Mode, the following functions are provided: Bob Weight, Force Fight Compensation, Configuration Trim, Yaw Damping and Turn Coordination, Mach Trim and Horizontal Stabilizer Auto Trim, Roll Assist, Roll/Speedbrake Mixer, Ground Lift Dump, and Pitch trim rate adjustment depending on airspeed.

TAWS provides these visual and aural alert messages:
- Collision Prediction Alerting (CPA) CAUTION OBSTACLE GND PROX (amber): The aircraft will impact the obstacle in 40 s to 60 s. The obstacle is displayed in amber on the map.
- Collision Prediction Alerting (CPA) Warning OBSTACLE AHEAD, PULL UP PULL UP (red): The aircraft approaches predictive impact of an obstacle. The obstacle is displayed in red on the map.
- Collision Prediction Alerting (CPA) Warning AVOID OBSTACLE PULL UP (red): The aircraft approaches predictive impact of an obstacle. The obstacle is displayed in red on the map.
- Collision Prediction Alerting (CPA) Caution CAUTION TERRAIN GND PROX (amber): Predicated impact with terrain to occur is 40 s to 60 s away. The obstacle is displayed in amber on the map.
- Collision Prediction Alerting (CPA) Warning - Pull Up TERRAIN AHEAD,PULL UP PULL UP (red): The aircraft approaches predictive impact of an obstacle. The aircraft is approaching the terrain. The obstacle is displayed in red.
- Collision Prediction Alerting (CPA) Warning - Terrain Avoidance AVOID TERRAIN PULL UP (red): The aircraft approaches predictive impact of an obstacle. The aircraft is approaching the terrain. The obstacle is displayed in red.
- Mode 1 Caution SINK RATE GND PROX (amber): Excessive rate of descent.
- Mode 1 Warning WHOOP, WHOOP, PULL UP PULL UP (red): Excessive descent rate increased to severe descent rate. It is displayed after “SINK RATE” aural alert occurs.
- Mode 2 Caution TERRAIN, TERRAIN GND PROX (amber): Dangerous proximity to terrain with a high closure rate. If in landing configuration with gear down and flaps extended a continuous aural caution alert TERRAIN will sound.
- Mode 2 Warning WHOOP, WHOOP, PULL UP PULL UP (red): Dangerous proximity to terrain with a high closure rate. It is displayed after “TERRAIN， TERRAIN” aural alert occurs.
- Mode 3 Caution DON'T SINK, DON'T SINK GND PROX (amber): Altitude decreases during takeoff or go-around.
- Mode 4 Caution TOO LOW TERRAIN GND PROX (amber), TOO LOW GEAR GND PROX (amber), TOO LOW FLAPS GND PROX (amber): The aircraft is in an incorrect landing configuration and the terrain clearance is insufficient.
- Mode 5 Caution GLIDE SLOPE GND PROX (amber): Excessive G/S deviation.
- Bank Angle Alert BANK ANGLE, BANK ANGLE: Excessive bank angle.
- Windshear Caution CAUTION WINDSHEAR WINDSHEAR (amber): Headwind increases (or tailwind decreases) and rising air movement is detected.
- Windshear Warning WINDSHEAR, WINDSHEAR, WINDSHEAR WINDSHEAR (red): Headwind decreases (or tailwind increases) and downward air movement is detected.

Stall Protection System (SPS) Ice Advance Mode 2 activates if the ice detector on either side detects ice, the wing anti-ice system is available, and the STALL ADVANCE Switch is released. It also activates if the ice detector on either side detects ice, the wing anti-ice system fails, and the STALL ADVANCE Switch is released. After activation, SPS Ice Advance Mode 2 remains active even if the conditions are no longer met, unless a higher priority mode is triggered. To exit Ice Advance Mode 2, the STALL ADVANCE Switch must be cycled when the flap is down and the aircraft is in level flight. When the WING A/I Switch is engaged, SPS automatically enters Ice Advance Mode 2 and will remain in this mode even if the WING A/I Switch is disengaged. If the STALL ADVANCE Switch is pushed manually while in Ice Advance Mode 2, the system enters ADVANCE ON Mode. If the STALL ADVANCE Switch is released manually, the system reverts to normal mode or Advance On Mode based on current status.
To exit Ice Advance Mode 2, when flap is down and the aircraft is in level flight, cycle the STALL ADVANCE Switch.

The primary flight control system automatically reverts from Normal Mode to Direct Mode when two out of three sets of valid airspeed data sources are lost, or both Flight Control Cabinets (FCCs) fail or lose power.

The Stall Protection System (SPS) enters Flap/Slat Fail Advance Mode in any of the following conditions: Flap system fails on FSECU bus, and flap configuration is not in 0. Flap system fails on FSECU bus or slat angle on both sides is not available, and flap configuration is not in 0. The slat angle difference between the two sides is 3° for 5 s, and flap configuration is not in 0.

During the final approach phase of a localizer-based approach, the FMS configures for a NAV-to-NAV transfer, tunes both navigation receivers to the localizer frequency, and displays LOC armed on the PFD with the localizer inbound course on the HSI. The FMS remains in TERM mode until localizer signal capture and then switches to localizer signal for steering guidance. Lateral deviation scaling is set to ±1.0 NM, and vertical deviation scaling remains at ±500 ft. Once the localizer signal is captured, the FMS continues to provide Baro-VNAV vertical guidance down to, but not past, the FAF. For an ILS approach, the FCS switches from FMS vertical guidance to the ILS glideslope upon interception.

The shakers vibrate twice for approximately 2 s each time before the stick pusher activates. They activate again when the airframe AOA is above the threshold of the stick shaker and deactivate when the airframe AOA is less than the threshold of the stick shaker decreased by 0.5°.

If the AOA continues to increase beyond the shaker level after the stick shakers are activated, the Stall Protection Computer (SPC) will automatically send a push command to the pitch servo, causing the control column to move forward to prevent aircraft stall.

Refueling is normally done by pressure, with a maximum pressure of 55 psi. Gravity refueling is an alternative if pressure equipment is unavailable. There are two modes of pressure refueling: automatic and manual, selected by the REFUEL SELECTION Switch. In automatic mode, the Fuel Quantity Computer (FQC) monitors and controls the shutoff valves based on a preselected quantity, ensuring fuel balance between tanks. In manual mode, refueling personnel manually control the Refuel Shutoff Valve. The High Level Float Pilot Valve will always close the Refuel Shutoff Valve when maximum quantity is reached.

The Thrust Lever has five positions: Maximum Thrust (MAX), Takeoff/Go-around (TO/GA), IDLE, Minimum Reverse Thrust (MIN REV), and Maximum Reverse Thrust (MAX REV). The Thrust Lever is equipped with a Reverser Lock, which prevents the Thrust Lever from moving to reverse position until certain conditions are satisfied. After all wheels touchdown, the reverser lock unlocks automatically, enabling the pilot to pull the thrust reverser trigger and set the thrust lever to the reverse position. Thrust control has two modes: Automatic mode (Autothrottle System manages thrust) and Manual mode (pilot manually controls thrust).
